MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE HELD IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  OF THE LA VERNE CITY HALL
  Monday, April 15, 2019

1.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Kendrick at 6: 30 p. m., and he
  welcomed everyone to the City Council Meeting.

2  Council Members present:  Mayor pon Kendrick
  Mayor Pro Tem Charlie Rosales
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Muir Davis
  Council Member Tim Hepburn

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Manager/ Public Works Director Dan Keesey
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Community Deve opment Director Eric Scherer
  Community Services Director Bill Aguirre
  Police Chief Nick Paz
  Interim Fire Chief Kirk Summers
  Police Captain Coleen Flores
  Personnel Officer JR Ranelts

3  Pledge of Aliegiance was led by Mayor Kendrick.

4.  Presentation of Prociamation  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, presented La Verne Police
  dec aring the week of  Communications Supervisor Rebekah Biedermann a Proclamation declaring

  Public  Safety  Week to honor the men and women in our community who respond to
  Telecommunicators Week  emergency calls, dispatch emergency professionals and equipment, and
  render lifesaving assistance to the citizens of La Verne.

  La Verne Police Communications Supervisor Biedermann thanked the City
  Council for honoring the Public Safety Telecomunicators.

  Police Chief Paz also commended the Public Safety Telecomunicators for the
  awesome job they do serving the citizens of the La Verne and he stated it is
  the hardest job in the department.

5  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Rosales, and unanimously carried to
  accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items.

  Project  The Public Works Department recently solicited bids for street maintenance at
  various locations throughout the City. The planned maintenance for the
  majority of the streets will include the removal and replacement of two inches
  of asphalt with the addition of an Asphalt- Rubber Aggregate Membrane
  ARAM), while Bowdoin Street from Emerald Avenue to Fruit Street will receive
  an application of slurry seal. The project was advertised on February 22 and
  March 1 and bid proposals were received and opened on March 21, 2019. This
  project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act,
  Section 15301 -  Existing Facilities, and City of La Verne environmental
  guidelines.

  Staff recommended that the City Council approve Resolution No. 19- 15, which
  awards a public works contract to Gentry Brothers Construction Inc., the lowest,
  responsible bidder in the amount of$ 425, 802. 50. Approved as
  recommended by staff.

6.  2019- 20 Paramedic Service Fee  Finance Manager Statham reported on the Paramedic Service Fee for fiscal
  year 2019- 20. He stated that the City's voter approved Paramedic Service Fee
  requires an annual hearing in order to consider a change in rate. The monthly
  service fee is subject to annual adjustment to changes in the Consumer Price
  Index. Since October 2018, Consumer Price Index had a 3. 5%  change, and

  the monthly rate can be adjusted by $ 0. 18 to $ 5. 37. Staff recommended that
  the City Council adjust the monthly paramedic service fee from $ 5. 19 to$ 5. 37.

  Mayor Kendrick opened the public hearing and called for public comment on
  this matter.

  Gary Hunter, Chelsea Drive, La Verne, stated that it is pretty cheap insurance
  and the adjustment should be more.

  Heather Gay, La Verne resident, stated that she has used the paramedic
  service in the past 22 months and praised the amazing men and women for
  the great work they do and that she fully endorsed the program.

  The City Council praised and commended the La Verne paramedics and that
  they fully supported the paramedic service program.

  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Davis, and unanimously carried to
  adopt Resolution No. 19- 16, adjusting the monthly paramedic service fee from
  5. 19 to$ 5. 37.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 15, 2019, Page 3

  Resolution  No.  19- 16  Resolution No. 19- 16 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF
  CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING THE PARAMEDIC SERVICE FEE FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2019- 20. Approved.

7.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Kendrick called for
  public comment.

  Joyce Kelly, La Verne resident, stated that the building on the corner of Foothill
  and Wheeler Avenue is an eyesore and asked what is being doing. She stated
  she found out a Taco Bell fast food restaurant will be at the site and that the
  majority of residents don' t want another Mexican restaurant.  She stated that it
  was bit too much with other similar businesses in the vicinity. She stated she
  was glad the lawsuit with the La Verne Firefighters' Association is over. She
  spoke about the time line of the events leading to the lawsuit and stated that
  the cost and expense was not good for the City.

  Hugh Kelly, La Verne resident, thanked the Parks Department for cutting the
  grass at the building on the corner of Foothill and Wheeler. He spoke about
  the La Verne Firefighters' Association settlement and the team building to
  make La Verne a better place.

  Pam Berry, La Verne resident, announced that the La Verne Coalition of
  Concerned Citizens ( LV3C) which was launched in October, to increase
  transparency and to encoura ge residents to participate and to make the City
  4t

  the best can be, meets the  Monday of each month at 7: 00 pm. She stated
  that on April 22, 2019, Mayor Kendrick will be delivering the State of City
  address at Saint John' s Episcopal Church and stated that she has flyers with
  additional information and will be available after the meeting.

  Brain Bowcock, La Verne resident, commended and thanked Police Chief Nick
  Paz, Police and Captain Coleen Flores for the amazing job the Police RSVP
  did during the Community Yard sale and that is what La Verne is all about.

  Gary Hunter, La Verne resident, asked what could be done with the homeless
  camping out at Emerald Park.

  City Manager Russi replied he should call the La Verne Police Department
  who will assist the homeless in seeking the needed services.

  Rick McGueron, La Verne resident stated that in the interest of transparency
  he would like to see on the Agenda the lawsuit settlement with the La Verne
  Firefighters' Association and that the public be given an explanation on why
  the decision to settle was made.

  Susan Morales, La Verne resident spoke at length about the wireless 5g small
  cell towers health exposure to the public if installed on City street light poles.
  She urged the City Council to further study this matter before implementing
  installation of wireless 5g small cell towers.
   City Council Minutes. Monday, April 15, 2019, Page 4

  Richard Bowen, La Verne resident stated it was great to hear all the accolades
  for the Police and Fire Departments. He spoke about the La Verne
  Firefighters' Association lawsuit and the chain of events that started in May of
  2017, with the vote of no confidence of the Fire Chief and how the City did
  nothing. He stated that the Battalion Fire Chief who videotaped and took
  photos is still on the City' s payrofl along with the Fire Chief and now the City
  settled for$ 5. 5 million. He stated that the City should apologize for letting this
  happen. He spoke about the Fire Association supporting a Mayor candidate
  that was not the sitting Mayor. He asked about the whereabouts of the Fire
  Chief and why has he not been fired. He stated " Shame on the Council for
  doing nothing when the vote of no confidence was presented. He stated that
  Resolution No. 18- 51 &  18- 52 should be rescinded to get all Council members
  back to work. He urged the City Council to take the following actions, find a
  new City Attorney; thank him for his 28 years of service and give him a plaque,
  name a bench after him and fire the City Manager without severance pay for
  the alleged lies he told the newspaper. Ne stated if Council did nothing, they
  would find people who will.

  Tom Skahill, La Verne resident, reminded everyone it was tax day and that it is
  also National Donate a Life Month. He urged people to check the box on their
  driver license to be an organ donor and help save a life.

8  Council Comments and  Council Member Hepburn reported on the following:
  Meeting/ Conference Reports
  Foothill Terrace Emergency Preparedness Day. He was amazed how well
  prepared they are for an emergency and he spoke about the amazing
  qualifications of the individuals running the program. He stated he brought
  emergency checklists forms and they will be available at the end of the
  meeting.

  General Assembly of the San Gabriel Council of Governments and the
  many topics addressed at the meeting.

  La Verne San Dimas Educational Golf Tournament to be held on April 26,
  2019 and invited the public to sign- up and additional information will be
  available on the City' s website.

  La Verne Police Officers' Association Golf Tournament on May 20, 2019
  and he reported that the proceeds from the event would go to the Youth
  and Family Action Committee.

  v  Easter Egg Hunt at Las Flores and Emerald Park on Saturday, April 19,
  2019, and the car show on the same day.

  He wished everyone a Happy Easter and thanked everyone for coming.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales wished everyone a Happy Easter.

  Council Member Davis urged the residents to be patient, that information will
  come out in due time and not to listen to people who think they know the facts.
  He wished everyone a Happy Easter and all the Blessings from above.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, April 15, 2019, Page 5

  Council Member Carder stated that the City Council wants to move forward
  and work with the community and Fire Association to make La Verne a better
  place. She stated that information on the lawsuit is on the Federal Courts
  website and urged the residents to go online.

  Council Member Carder reported on the car show to be held on Saturday, April
  20, 2019. She reminded everyone of the Gold Line Meeting regarding the
  Draft Environmental Impact Report on the Foothill Gold Line Extension and of
  the City Council Gold Line Study Session on April 29, 2019, when City Staff
  will give a presentation to the City Council on the Draft Environmental Impact
  Report on the Foothill Gold Line Extension. She wished everyone a Happy
  Easter and to be safe.

  Mayor Kendrick also reported on the Foothill Terrace Mobile Home Park
  Emergency Preparedness' Day and he spoke about the Community
  Emergency Response Team ( CERT) Program which now has 152 members in
  the Community including several members from Foothill Terrace Mobile Home
  Park. He spoked about the Firefighters' Association lawsuit and how hard
  Staff tried to resolve the matter, but the parties, sadly, did not get together until
  the court day. He too, urged the residents to go on the Federal Courts website
  and get the information and judge for themselves. He stated they need to
  move forward as a City.

  Council Member Hepburn also spoke about the Community Emergency
  Response Team and that Mr. and Mrs. Kestersons who run the CERT program
  reside at Foothill Terrace Mobile Home Park. He reported that the Friends of
  the La Verne Library are still looking for new board members and officers and
  that they can contact La Verne Library Manager George May, if they are
  interested in serving. In addition, he stated that the Firefighters' Association
  lawsuit was a very difficult time, and was difficult for him too. He was not
  happy with the settlement, and the cost. He was glad it was over, and urged
  the public to read the depositions to get the full facts.

  Council Member Carder reported on the " Tip a Cop" event held at Mi Ranchito
  Restaurant. She stated it was a wonderful event and the Police Officers raised
  2500 for the Special Olympics. She thanked and commended the Police
  Officers who participated in the event.

9  Adjournment at 7: 29 pm., in memory  of Thomas Albin Gay, fondly known as " Tom" who passed away on

  March 11, 2019. Tom was a native of La Verne, attended Roynon Elementary School, Bonita High School and
  Cal Poly Pomona. Tom' s father owned and managed the Richfield Gas Station on the southwest corner of
  Bonita Avenue ( called 4th Street then) and " D" Street, currently now the Miss Doughnut Shoppe. Tom and
  his many buddies watched from Bonita High the filming of the famous last Church scene of the " The Graduate"
  in 1967. Tom was a member of La Verne Historical Society and was the point person for the Bonita High
  School 10- year reunions. Tom was a Renaissance man who did everything and did it well. He is survived by his
  wife Heather and; The City Council adjourned to Monday, April 29, 2019, at 4: 30 pm., for Staff presentation
  on the Draft Environmental Impact Report on the Foothill Gold Line Extension.
